about.text: Extended shelf life milk: heated higher than pasteurised milk, to about 120–135 °C for a second or two, or filtered through fine membranes, so that unopened in the fridge it keeps for about three weeks while tasting close to fresh milk.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Microfilter, then pasteurise at 72–85 °C (72 °C for 15–20 s). A 1.4 µm microfilter removes up to 99.99 % of bacteria and spores

Raw milk is separated; skim goes through a ceramic membrane (nominal 1.4 µm); the germ-rich retentate is either removed or mixed with the cream and UHT-treated (135–150 °C, 2–3 s); the fat is set again and the milk pasteurised; total reduction 4.6–5.6 log units (Frontiers in Microbiology review, 2017)
1.4 µm gives up to 99.99 % fewer bacteria and spores; 0.8 µm gives 99.9999 % (Tetra Pak)
Tetra Pak: remixing MF retentate into the milk is not recommended for ESL milk (it is common in cheese milk)
A centrifuge that spins out spores is not enough to go beyond 14 days, even double (Tetra Pak)
